observations.text: Revenue CAGR 9.9% and PAT CAGR 13.6% over FY15-FY26.
FY26 ROIC is 7.2%; rolling 3y incremental ROIC swung 4.0%-18.9%, latest window 10.8%.
Interest coverage 4.5x on FY26 borrowings of Rs 4,02,962 cr.

inferences.text: Returns sit near or below a reasonable WACC — this is a capital-heavy compounder whose growth is bought with balance sheet, not earned cheaply.

open_questions: Split of maintenance vs growth capex (screener does not disclose it).
Segment-level ROIC — retail/Jio vs O2C — which the consolidated number hides.
financial_statement_analyst.disconfirming_search: Checked whether low ROIC is a one-off: it is structural across all 11 years, not a single bad year.
financial_statement_analyst.narrative: At ROIC ~7%, Reliance is not a high-quality self-funding compounder at the consolidated level; its growth has been financed by heavy reinvestment and borrowing. Incremental ROIC never durably clears mid-teens, so each new rupee of capital earns modestly.

observations.text: Cumulative CFO/PAT 1.71 over 11 years; FY26 CFO/PAT 2.01 — reported profit converts to cash.
CWIP fell from 33% of assets (FY15) to 10.9% (FY26) — capex commissioned into productive assets, not perpetual work-in-progress.

inferences.text: No cash-reality red flags: the cash is real and the cash-flow statement agrees with the P&L.

open_questions: Related-party transaction map across the subsidiary structure not yet mapped from filings.
forensic_accountant.disconfirming_search: Tested the classic manipulation tells (cash not converting, ageing CWIP, cash-vs-interest): none fired on the deterministic screen.
forensic_accountant.narrative: Forensic deterministic screen returns PASS. The earnings-to-cash conversion is strong and the CWIP that ballooned during the Jio/refinery build has since commissioned - the opposite of the perpetual-CWIP siphoning pattern. No veto.

open_questions: Would a segment-level SOTP show a high-ROIC business the consolidated average masks?
thesis_synthesizer.disconfirming_search: Looked for a self-funding path at a lower target: even a 2x/6y (12.2% CAGR) needs ~1.7x reinvestment - still external-funding dependent at 7.2% ROIC.
thesis_synthesizer.narrative: As a multibagger candidate under the firm's one question, Reliance does NOT clear the self-funding feasibility gate: its ROIC is too low to fund the growth a 4x demands. It is a fine business with real cash, but the arithmetic says a 5-10x self-funded compound is not the live scenario here. NOTE: Reliance is far outside the firm's Rs300-30000cr universe - used here only to demonstrate the machinery end-to-end on real data.
thesis_synthesizer.return_multiple_if: A 4x-in-6y case requires ~26% earnings CAGR; at 7.2% ROIC that needs 3.6x NOPAT reinvested — only possible with large external equity/debt and the dilution that implies.
three_load_bearing_assumptions: A structural ROIC inflection (retail/Jio mix lifting consolidated returns) - not yet in the numbers.
External funding at non-dilutive terms - contradicted by the 3.6x reinvestment requirement.
Re-rating argued separately from growth - no identified driver at current returns.
thesis_synthesizer.feasibility_verdict: NEEDS_EXTERNAL_FUNDING (fails the self-funding test for a 4x/6y target at current ROIC)
